title: Algolia search-only API key: documented frontend use against documented exposure risk
summary: A search-only API key in frontend code, in a request header or in a repository: the evidence documents both that the key is meant for production frontend code and that an exposed key lets third parties scrape the indices and flood the account.
rationale: Claim search-only-api-key-exposure records both statements, and claims search-only-api-key-restricted-derivation-and-mitigation and search-only-api-key-referrer-restriction-is-light record Algolia's mitigation advice. Whether a detection of such a key in public code is a finding is an exposure-policy question the contract says it does not answer (open-question-3). The ACL set of the predefined key is not stated (open-question-5), the role is attributable from context only because the header and any value shape are shared with every other role (open-question-2), the application ID beside it has no documented public status (open-question-6) and the era of the frontend-safe guidance is not dated (open-question-7). A must-flag would contradict the documented frontend intent; a must-not-flag would ignore the documented risk. Contract claims cited: search-only-api-key/search-only-api-key-exposure, search-only-api-key/search-only-api-key-restricted-derivation-and-mitigation.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. The value of a search-only key is recorded as unscored: a consumer neither gains nor loses a point on it. May-flag is not used: no maintainer decision states that either behaviour is acceptable, and the contract says the exposure-policy question is not answered. Settled by: an Algolia statement of the exposure policy or of the ACL set of the predefined key, or a maintainer's recorded policy decision.

sources.supports: It works on all your Algolia application indices and is safe to use in your production frontend code. When using Algolia, your search-only API key is exposed and third parties could use it to: Scrape everything from your indices; Flood your account with search requests.
It works on all your Algolia application indices and is safe to use in your production frontend code. You may want to use this key to create more restricted API keys.
Ensure your indices only contain data you’re happy to expose. Generate and use a secured search-only API key with rate-limiting, index access, and other restrictions.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. No expectation is asserted and no value was built: the record states what the cited contract settles and what it leaves open. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
